method: Page fetched directly with curl and converted from HTML to text (no intermediate scraper), collapsing whitespace and removing the space left before punctuation where a link tag closes mid-sentence. Every claim below is verbatim-checked against that file with scripts/verify.py.

claims.claim: First published 2017 and revised 2024, eight quality statements
claims.source_text: The Osteoarthritis of the Knee Clinical Care Standard was first published in 2017 and revised in 2024 … eight quality statements for safe and appropriate care

claims.claim: The Standard originated in the 2015 Atlas finding on knee arthroscopy variation
claims.source_text: The Osteoarthritis of the Knee Clinical Care Standard was first released in 2017 in response to findings from the 2015 Australian Atlas of Healthcare Variation (the Atlas). The Atlas identified considerable variation in rates of knee arthroscopy in Australia, despite the limited value of this intervention for degenerative disease due to knee osteoarthritis

claims.claim: Indicator 8a is expressed as a number
claims.source_text: Number of patients who have undergone arthroscopic procedures to treat uncomplicated knee osteoarthritis

claims.claim: Indicators 2a to 2d measure diagnosis without imaging
claims.source_text: Proportion of patients diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis without imaging … Proportion of patients diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis without magnetic resonance imaging … Proportion of patients diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis without computerised tomography scan … Proportion of patients diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis without ultrasound

claims.claim: Statement 1 text
claims.source_text: A patient with suspected knee osteoarthritis receives a comprehensive, person-centred assessment which includes a detailed history of the presenting symptoms, comorbidities, a physical examination, and a psychosocial evaluation of factors affecting quality of life and participation in activities. A diagnosis of knee osteoarthritis can be confidently made based on this assessment

claims.claim: Diagnosis can be made without imaging
claims.source_text: If the clinical signs, symptoms, and findings of a comprehensive assessment are typical of knee osteoarthritis, a diagnosis can be made without imaging or further investigations

claims.claim: Physical examination components
claims.source_text: the patient's gait, range of motion, joint line tenderness, malalignment or deformities, bony enlargement, effusion, restricted movement, and crepitus

claims.claim: Atypical features suggesting an alternative diagnosis
claims.source_text: a history of past trauma to the knee … malignancy … prolonged morning joint-related stiffness … rapidly worsening symptoms or the presence of a hot swollen joint … whether pain may be referred from hip or spine pathology

claims.claim: Misconceptions and unhelpful beliefs are to be addressed
claims.source_text: Identify and address with the patient any misconceptions and unhelpful beliefs about knee osteoarthritis, its management, trajectory, and treatments

claims.claim: Statement 2 text
claims.source_text: Imaging is not routinely used to diagnose knee osteoarthritis and is not offered to a patient with suspected knee osteoarthritis. When clinically warranted, X-ray is the first-line imaging. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), computerised tomography (CT) and ultrasound are not appropriate investigations to diagnose knee osteoarthritis

claims.claim: Detecting meniscal tears may lead to inappropriate arthroscopy
claims.source_text: degenerative meniscal tears are common in osteoarthritic knees, whether people have symptoms or not. Therefore, detection of meniscal tears does not provide useful additional information and may lead people to pursue inappropriate management such as arthroscopy

claims.claim: Pain and structural change correlate poorly
claims.source_text: Patients may experience substantial pain with only minor structural changes to joints identified on imaging, while minimal symptoms may accompany more notable (though modest) structural changes

claims.claim: Response when a patient requests imaging
claims.source_text: If a patient with suspected knee osteoarthritis requests diagnostic imaging, ask about their concerns and their expectations of imaging. Reassure them that having X-rays or other diagnostic imaging will not change initial treatment, which will be guided by their mobility and function

claims.claim: MRI reports should lead with knee osteoarthritis over meniscal tear
claims.source_text: when knee osteoarthritis is observed on MRI, including thinning of the cartilage or degenerative meniscal changes including tears, a finding of 'knee osteoarthritis' should be included in the report. This is of greater clinical relevance than the presence of a meniscal tear

claims.claim: Statement 3 text
claims.source_text: Information about knee osteoarthritis and treatment options is discussed with the patient. The patient participates in developing an individualised self management plan that addresses their physical, functional, and psychosocial health needs

claims.claim: Self-management plan contents
claims.source_text: strategies to support increased physical activity participation such as pacing activities, management of painful episodes and flares, and pain management techniques … strategies for protecting the knee joints such as the use of walking aids … weight management and nutrition guidance

claims.claim: Statement 4 text
claims.source_text: A patient with knee osteoarthritis is advised that being active can help manage knee pain and improve function … The patient is encouraged to set exercise and physical activity goals and is recommended services or programs to help them achieve their goals

claims.claim: Exercise will not cause damage
claims.source_text: Reassure the patient that exercise will not cause damage and is not a risky activity

claims.claim: Pain during exercise does not mean damage
claims.source_text: Feeling some pain or discomfort when exercising is normal and does not mean it is damaging your knee joint

claims.claim: Exercise is safe even in severe disease
claims.source_text: Exercise is safe for your knee, even if you have severe knee osteoarthritis

claims.claim: Activity may reduce medicines and avoid surgery
claims.source_text: Changes in activity may reduce the need for medicines and avoid surgery, as well as help patients manage chronic comorbidities and improve their overall health

claims.claim: Nine out of 10 can manage without joint replacement
claims.source_text: Nine out of 10 people with knee osteoarthritis can manage without needing joint replacement surgery

claims.claim: Passive manual therapies have no significant role
claims.source_text: Passive manual therapies, such as therapeutic ultrasound and electrotherapy, do not play a significant role in the treatment of knee osteoarthritis

claims.claim: Factors reviewed when setting activity goals
claims.source_text: Review factors such as the physical home environment, level of support, cultural activities, access to safe spaces to exercise, falls risk, and attitudes towards physical activity

claims.claim: Statement 5 text
claims.source_text: A patient with knee osteoarthritis is advised of the impact of body weight on symptoms. The patient is offered support to manage their weight and optimise nutrition that is tailored to their priorities and preferences

claims.claim: 5 to 10% weight loss over 20 weeks
claims.source_text: If the patient is living with excess weight, advise them that a 5–10% or greater weight loss over a 20-week period is associated with reduced pain and improved quality of life

claims.claim: Weight loss reduces pain and may reduce need for medicines or surgery
claims.source_text: Loss of excess weight reduces knee pain and improves function for patients with knee osteoarthritis, and can improve other comorbidities. These changes may reduce the need for medicines or knee surgery

claims.claim: Weight discussions to be sensitive and non-judgemental
claims.source_text: Acknowledge to the patient the challenges of losing weight and any previous weight loss attempts. Communicate in a sensitive, empathetic, and non‑judgemental way about how losing excess weight or maintaining weight will help them

claims.claim: BMI may not be the appropriate measure
claims.source_text: Body mass index (BMI) may not always be an appropriate measure for indicating whether a patient is above a healthy weight; other measures may be used, including body composition measurements or waist circumference

claims.claim: Weight loss can improve eligibility for surgery
claims.source_text: If a patient living with excess weight is considering or seeking surgery, explain that weight loss can improve their eligibility for surgery, reduce risks, and improve outcomes

claims.claim: Statement 6 text forbids opioids
claims.source_text: A patient with knee osteoarthritis is offered medicines to manage their pain and mobility in accordance with the current version of the Therapeutic Guidelines or locally endorsed, evidence-based guidelines. A patient is not offered opioid analgesics for knee osteoarthritis because the risk of harm outweighs the benefits

claims.claim: Do not offer opioid analgesics
claims.source_text: Do not offer opioid analgesics to patients with knee osteoarthritis. Opioids have significant risk of harm which outweigh potential benefits in pain management for knee osteoarthritis

claims.claim: The narrow opioid exception
claims.source_text: Opioid analgesics may have a role in very limited circumstances. For example, this may include short‑term use in patients with severe persisting pain not relieved by first-line medicines and optimal non‑surgical interventions, and who are awaiting non‑general practitioner specialist review

claims.claim: Taper if already prescribed
claims.source_text: If a patient is already using an opioid analgesic to treat knee osteoarthritis, discuss changes in therapy with them and explain the risks and need to start tapering the dose with a view to stopping the medicine

claims.claim: Six named treatments not recommended
claims.source_text: Do not offer platelet-rich plasma (PRP), hyaluronan, stem cell treatments, medicinal cannabis, gabapentin or pregabalin, as they are not recommended in knee osteoarthritis

claims.claim: Medicines should not replace self-management
claims.source_text: Ensure they understand that medicines should not replace self‑management strategies, including physical activity

claims.claim: Medicine recommendations are in the Standard itself
claims.source_text: Recommendations regarding use of medicines in knee osteoarthritis are described in the Standard

claims.claim: Aboriginal patients more than twice as likely to be prescribed opioids
claims.source_text: Consider the variation in pharmacological pain management for Aboriginal patients, with studies showing Aboriginal patients are more than twice as likely to be prescribed opioids in primary care than non-Aboriginal patients

claims.claim: Statement 7 text
claims.source_text: A patient with knee osteoarthritis receives planned clinical review at agreed intervals, and management is adjusted for any changing needs. A patient who has worsening symptoms and severe functional impairment that persists despite optimal non‑surgical management is referred for assessment to a non‑general practitioner (GP) specialist or multidisciplinary service

claims.claim: A dedicated appointment for each review
claims.source_text: Dedicate an appointment to each review

claims.claim: Review components
claims.source_text: monitoring symptoms and response to treatment, using the same tools as used at the initial assessment (such as PROMs) … reviewing all prescription, over-the-counter, and complementary medicines the patient may be using … evaluating any side effects from treatment

claims.claim: Weight-bearing X-ray at referral
claims.source_text: weight-bearing X-ray imaging of the knee

claims.claim: Specialist referral options and deferral to the RACGP guideline
claims.source_text: non‑general practitioner specialist assessment, such as a rheumatologist, orthopaedic surgeon, or sports and exercise physician. If referring to an orthopaedic surgeon for assessment, follow recommendations for referral in the RACGP Guideline for the management of knee and hip osteoarthritis

claims.claim: Review interval decided with the patient
claims.source_text: Decide with the patient how regularly they need a review of their knee osteoarthritis

claims.claim: Statement 8 text
claims.source_text: A patient with knee osteoarthritis who has severe functional impairment despite optimal non-surgical management is considered for timely joint replacement surgery or joint-conserving surgery. The patient receives comprehensive information about the procedure and potential outcomes to inform their decision. Arthroscopic procedures are not offered to treat uncomplicated knee osteoarthritis

claims.claim: 12 weeks of optimal physical activity and exercise
claims.source_text: Assess whether the patient has undertaken optimal non‑surgical management, such as 12 weeks of optimal physical activity and exercise

claims.claim: Do not offer arthroscopy for uncomplicated knee osteoarthritis
claims.source_text: Do not offer arthroscopic procedures as treatment for uncomplicated knee osteoarthritis

claims.claim: Arthroscopy provides little or no clinically significant benefit
claims.source_text: Arthroscopic procedures, including debridement and partial meniscectomy, provide little or no clinically significant benefit in pain or function and are not indicated as a primary treatment in the management of uncomplicated knee osteoarthritis

claims.claim: Uncomplicated is defined, and meniscal tears do not warrant arthroscopy
claims.source_text: Uncomplicated knee osteoarthritis is not accompanied by true mechanical locking, septic arthritis, or inflammatory arthropathy. Meniscal changes, such as tears identified by imaging, do not warrant arthroscopy

claims.claim: When arthroscopy may be indicated
claims.source_text: Arthroscopy may be indicated if the patient has an alternate diagnosis such as true mechanical locking, septic arthritis, or inflammatory arthropathy requiring synovectomy

claims.claim: PROMs before and after all surgical interventions
claims.source_text: Use PROMs before and after all surgical interventions

claims.claim: Scope is patients aged 45 and over
claims.source_text: This Standard relates to the care that patients aged 45 years and over should receive when they present with knee pain and are suspected of having knee osteoarthritis

claims.claim: Out of scope items
claims.source_text: management of knee pain in people aged under 45 years … management of knee pain due to recent trauma or with symptoms that are not suggestive of knee osteoarthritis and where another diagnosis is suspected … rehabilitation after knee surgery

claims.claim: Prevalence increases sharply from age 45 and is higher in women
claims.source_text: Knee osteoarthritis is more common in women than men and, although it may affect people of all ages, the prevalence increases sharply from the age of 45 years

claims.claim: No benchmarks are set by the Commission
claims.source_text: No benchmarks are set for these indicators by the Commission

claims.claim: Indicator 1a
claims.source_text: Proportion of patients newly diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis who had a comprehensive person-centred assessment

claims.claim: Indicators 3a to 3c
claims.source_text: Proportion of patients with knee osteoarthritis who have an individualised self-management plan … Proportion of patients with knee osteoarthritis whose individualised self-management plan includes documented advice on physical activity … Proportion of patients with knee osteoarthritis who are overweight whose individualised self-management plan includes documented advice on weight management

claims.claim: Indicator 6a is an arrangements indicator
claims.source_text: Evidence of local arrangements to ensure patients with knee osteoarthritis are prescribed or recommended medicines in accordance with the current Therapeutic Guidelines or locally endorsed, evidence-based guidelines

claims.claim: Indicator 7a
claims.source_text: Proportion of patients with knee osteoarthritis with a documented timeframe for review

claims.claim: Cultural safety recommendations are on page 8 of the downloadable Standard
claims.source_text: Refer to Recommendations on page 8 for considerations when providing care for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples
